# Kontour Design System

> **Status:** canonical design direction for Kontour product interfaces and brand usage.
> **Audience:** designers, engineers, product teams, and coding/design agents.
> **Core promise:** **Trust the work AI does.**

This file is the design constitution for Kontour AI. It follows the
[DESIGN.md format](https://github.com/google-labs-code/design.md): machine-readable tokens in
the front matter, roles and rules in the body. It was restructured from the owner-supplied
design draft (2026-09-27) and reconciled against the shipped `--k-*` token contract.

**This file states roles and rules. Values live in `tokens/`.** The front matter is generated
from `tokens/tokens.css`, `tokens/themes.css`, and `react/styles.css` by
`scripts/generate-design-md.mjs`; `npm run check:design` fails when it drifts. Change a value in
`tokens/`, then run `node scripts/generate-design-md.mjs --write`. Never hand-edit the front
matter. Prose restates a shipped value only as a backticked token name, an equals sign, and a
backticked value (optionally with a scope such as `(light)` or `(flow)` after the name); the
same check verifies every such quote against `tokens/`, and fails on any other value-looking
text that follows a token name on the same line (or in the same table cell).

Reading the packaged copy under `node_modules/@kontourai/ui/`: the generator script is not in
the package. The `tokens/*.css` files next to this file are the source of every value; the
front matter is a projection of them made before publishing.

### Authority

Precedence, highest first: approved canonical SVGs and tokens → this file → approved product
docs → existing, unsuperseded production patterns → reference artwork → generated concepts.
A shipped value is not an approved one: where a shipped token disagrees with this file, it is
recorded as OPEN and does not outrank the rule here. Generated images are references, not
production assets. A generated concept sheet is held privately by the owner; it is reference
only, never a production source.

Anything marked **OPEN** is unresolved. Do not silently resolve it in either direction: an
OPEN item records what ships today and where the design is headed, and both stay true until
someone decides. The full register is in [Open Decisions](#open-decisions).

### Reading the token block

The DESIGN.md format has no concept of modes or themes, so the generated keys encode them:

| Key shape | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | The CSS custom property minus `--k-`, dark default (`:root`) | `space-5` is `--k-space-5` |
| `name-light` | The value under `[data-theme="light"]` | `bg-light` |
| `name-<theme>` | The value under `.theme-<theme>` (dark) | `brand-flow` |
| `name-<theme>-light` | The value under `[data-theme="light"] .theme-<theme>` | `brand-flow-light` |

A reference such as `focus-ring: "{colors.brand}"` means "the brand value of the same mode and
theme", with a caveat from CSS: `--k-focus-ring` is declared once, on `:root`, as
`var(--k-brand)`, and custom properties inherit their computed value. It therefore follows a
theme's or light mode's brand only when the theme class and `data-theme` sit on the root
(`<html>`) element itself; on a descendant root, focus rings keep the default dark brand.
`primary` is not a CSS token; it is derived from whatever `.btn-primary` paints, so the format's
required `primary` color stays truthful (see OPEN-8).

Type levels (`display`, `title`, `body-md`, `label`, `eyebrow`, `badge`, `button`) are read from
the shipped selectors that use them, and `text-*` levels are the bare size steps. Components are
read from their classes in `react/styles.css`; properties that are shorthands or `calc()`
expressions, and rules inside `@media`, are left out rather than approximated. Tokens the format
cannot carry (font-family stacks, shadows, soft status fills, motion, stroke widths,
line-height and letter-spacing scales, stacking order) are listed with their values in a
comment at the end of the front matter, so the drift check covers every token.

The generator buckets each `--k-*` token by name pattern; an alias (`var(--k-other)`) takes its
target's bucket; any other token whose value is a literal hex or `rgb()`/`rgba()` color is
treated as a color. A token that fits none of these, or a token rule nested in an at-rule,
makes the generator fail until someone decides how this file represents it.

`npx @google/design.md lint DESIGN.md` reports every color that no generated component
references as an `orphaned-tokens` warning: default structure tokens such as `bg`, `line`,
`line-strong`, and `text-faint`, the status tones, and every light and theme variant. That is
expected: only five components are generated, for the dark default, and status tones are
consumed by tone classes rather than a component entry.

### Token architecture

The draft's direction: **primitive tokens → semantic tokens → component tokens → justified
product overrides**, and "components consume semantic tokens whenever practical." What ships
maps onto it only partly:

- **Primitive** (not shipped): there is no separate palette layer; `tokens/tokens.css` assigns
  literal values straight to semantic names. A named brand palette (Ink, Stone, product
  accents) is [#74](https://github.com/kontourai/ui/issues/74).
- **Semantic** (shipped, partly): the `--k-*` structure, text, status, and focus tokens. Explicit
  action and focus roles (`--k-action`, `--k-focus`), so that primary actions and focus stop
  borrowing the brand, are [#72](https://github.com/kontourai/ui/issues/72).
- **Component** (not shipped as tokens): primitives in `react/styles.css` read semantic tokens
  directly. The front matter's `components` entries are derived from those rules; they are
  not a separate token layer.
- **Justified product overrides** (shipped as theme classes): today a product theme overrides
  the brand slot, `--k-brand` and `--k-brand-contrast` (`.theme-console` overrides far more),
  and that slot also drives primary buttons and focus rings (OPEN-8).
  [#72](https://github.com/kontourai/ui/issues/72) makes the brand slot white-label-safe: a
  deployment overrides only the brand slot and every role stays correct.

Components consume semantic tokens. Do not scatter raw hex values, font sizes, arbitrary radii,
or one-off spacing through repositories; `npm run check:tokens` already forbids literal colors
in `react/styles.css`.

## Overview

Kontour AI makes software that helps end users understand, inspect, validate, and trust work
performed by AI. A contour makes hidden structure legible; Kontour applies that idea to AI
work:

> **Turn uncertainty into clarity.**

The product should not demand trust. It exposes enough evidence, provenance, state, and
explanation for users to establish justified confidence.

The brand feels precise, calm, rigorous, clear, capable, contemporary, and human; technical
without hype. Avoid cyberpunk, magical-AI imagery, surveillance aesthetics, fear, generic
enterprise SaaS, and complexity for its own sake.

Interfaces feel calm, deliberate, inspectable, organized, and information-rich without noise.

### The Kontour world

> **Kontour owns the terrain. Products own what happens within it.**

| Identity | Phenomenon | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kontour | Contour field resolving into clarity | AI work becoming legible |
| Station | S-shaped river or path | Orient, inspect, establish state |
| Flow | Directional movement | Work progressing through a system |
| Surface | Defined, exposed region | A complete state made visible |
| Future products | Purpose-specific phenomenon | Must map to actual behavior |

Products share a grammar (contour-derived geometry, compatible line weights, controlled
organic forms, environmental semantics, flat and monochrome viability, typography, and
restrained material depth), not one recolored icon.

**OPEN-9 — product endorsement form and hierarchy.** The company name is Kontour AI. How
products are named and endorsed under it is pending a brand-architecture decision. Don't
invent compound names that stack the company name, a product name, and "AI" or "Platform"
(e.g. "Kontour <Product> AI"); use the approved endorsement form once decided.

## Colors

Color roles, not values. The values for each mode and theme are in the front matter.

| Token | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `--k-bg` | Page canvas. |
| `--k-panel` | Default container surface. |
| `--k-panel-raised` | Raised or inset surface inside a panel (controls, nested regions). |
| `--k-line`, `--k-line-strong` | Hairline separation; `line-strong` for control borders and emphasis. |
| `--k-text`, `--k-text-muted` | Primary and secondary text. |
| `--k-text-faint` | Tertiary, non-essential text only. Meets WCAG AA for normal text on `--k-panel` in the default dark and light skins; it does not on `--k-panel-raised`, on the light `--k-bg`, or in `.theme-console`. Not machine-checked. |
| `--k-brand`, `--k-brand-contrast` | The product identity slot, and the text color that sits on it. |
| `--k-positive`, `--k-caution`, `--k-negative`, `--k-active`, `--k-neutral` | Shared status tones (see below). |
| `--k-*-soft` | Low-alpha tone fills behind status text; derived at runtime from the active tone. |
| `--k-focus-ring` | Keyboard focus affordance; an alias of `--k-brand` declared on `:root` (OPEN-8; see "Reading the token block" for where theme classes must sit). |

### Product color is identity, not status

Product accents express which product you are in. They never encode state, success, risk, or
confidence, and never form an implicit status scale in charts. Status uses the status tones.

The shared status scale maps product words to five tones: `positive`, `caution`, `negative`,
`active`, `neutral` (see `docs/adr/0001-console-kit-token-contract.md`). Never encode critical
state through color alone; status always carries text, and icon or color reinforces it.

**OPEN-7 — status model.** Shipped: the five tones above. Draft direction: distinct semantic
tokens for success, warning, danger, information, verified, uncertain, pending, unavailable,
and neutral, and a trust-state vocabulary (known, verified, inferred, estimated, uncertain,
conflicting, failed, unavailable, not checked) that must never collapse into one generic
confidence state. Tracked in [#73](https://github.com/kontourai/ui/issues/73). Until it ships,
map trust states onto the five tones *and* always name the state in text; never let two
different trust states render identically.

### Product themes

One theme class on a stable root selects the product identity (`docs/consumer-guide.md`):

- `.theme-flow`, `.theme-surface` override the brand slot only.
- `.theme-survey` overrides the brand slot plus canvas and faint text.
- `.theme-console` is a full skin: brand, surfaces, lines, text, status, radii, and its own
  font stacks.

**OPEN-6 — brand palette and product accents.** Shipped vs draft direction:

| Role | Shipped | Draft direction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Corporate ink | none; dark canvas `--k-bg` = `#0a0e13` | Ink `#0B1220` |
| Corporate light ground | none; light canvas `--k-bg` (light) = `#f5f4ef` | Stone `#F2EFEA`, White `#FFFFFF` |
| Station accent | no `theme-station` | `#7C3AED` |
| Flow accent | `--k-brand` (flow) = `#2f88a6`, `--k-brand` (flow-light) = `#1f6f88` | `#2563EB` |
| Surface accent | `--k-brand` (surface) = `#14a37a`, `--k-brand` (surface-light) = `#0f6b52` | `#14B8A6` |
| Default brand | `--k-brand` = `#5ce0c6`, `--k-brand` (light) = `#0e7c64` | not specified |

The draft's values are a palette, not tokens: do not add `--kontour-*` custom properties.
Migration to the brand palette is [#74](https://github.com/kontourai/ui/issues/74); final ramps
and dark-mode colors are also open.

**OPEN-10 — Console and Survey themes.** The draft does not cover `theme-console` or
`theme-survey`. They stay as shipped until the palette work decides their relationship to the
brand palette.

**OPEN-11 — marketing-site palette.** The relationship between these product tokens and the
marketing-site palette is undecided.

### Modes

**OPEN-5 — default mode.** Shipped: dark is the default (`:root`, `color-scheme: dark`) and
light is opt-in with `[data-theme="light"]`. Draft direction: light Stone/Ink as the default.
Until decided, keep the shipped contract and design every surface for both modes.

Dark mode is not inversion. Preserve hierarchy, restraint, product identity, contour
legibility, status semantics, and contrast. Ink may be preferable to pure black. Light-mode
status and brand hues are darkened so text clears WCAG AA on light panels; keep that property
when changing them (`npm run check:contrast`). Fine contour artwork may need optical adjustment
on dark surfaces. Final dark surface, text, and border ramps are OPEN.

## Typography

Three family roles:

| Token | Role | Draft role name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--k-font-display` | Display and titles: page headings, dialog titles. | `font-brand` |
| `--k-font-ui` | Interface text: controls, buttons, body. | `font-ui` |
| `--k-font-mono` | Identifiers, labels, badges, metadata, numerals in dense data. | `font-mono` |

Typography is precise, contemporary, calm, intelligent, slightly human, and highly legible.
Avoid sci-fi, techno, novelty-map, excessively geometric, and generic rounded SaaS faces.
Identifiers and technical values use the mono role and must wrap and copy gracefully.

**OPEN-4 — typefaces.** Shipped: Fraunces (display), Hanken Grotesk (UI), and IBM Plex Mono,
self-hosted in `tokens/fonts/`; `.theme-console` swaps display and UI for a condensed stack.
Draft direction: a humanist or restrained neo-grotesk with open counters, strong numerals,
excellent UI rendering, useful weights, and enough character to avoid sameness; final family
undecided. Generated concept typography is not a production font and not a wordmark.

**OPEN-3 — type scale.** Shipped steps run from `--k-text-xs` = `11px` to
`--k-text-2xl` = `clamp(26px, 3.4vw, 38px)`; the top step is fluid, and the front matter records
its upper bound. Draft direction, named levels (not shipped; do not
create these tokens):

| Draft level | Size / line | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| display-xl | 64 / 68 | major hero |
| display-lg | 48 / 52 | page hero |
| heading-xl | 36 / 42 | page heading |
| heading-lg | 28 / 34 | section heading |
| heading-md | 22 / 28 | panel heading |
| body-lg | 18 / 28 | emphasized prose |
| body-md | 16 / 24 | default body |
| body-sm | 14 / 20 | dense UI |
| label | 13 / 18 | controls, metadata |
| caption | 12 / 16 | secondary metadata |

Note that shipped control text is `--k-text-md` = `14px`, the size of the draft's `body-sm`.

Shipped styling sets `text-transform: uppercase` on buttons, badges, status labels, field
labels, eyebrows, panel headings, and titles (`.topbar h1`, `.dialog__title`). That is current
implementation, not a rule from the draft; keep it consistent until a typography decision
changes it.

### Wordmark

Primary naming: **Kontour AI**. Generated concept typography is not a production font or a
custom wordmark; production needs an approved family or a finalized vector wordmark (OPEN).

## Layout

Use a 4px base rhythm, and only the spacing tokens.

> **OPEN-1 — spacing scale. Danger: the same step numbers mean different sizes.**
>
> | Step | Shipped `--k-space-N` | Draft `space-N` |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | 1 | `--k-space-1` = `4px` | 4px |
> | 2 | `--k-space-2` = `8px` | 8px |
> | 3 | `--k-space-3` = `12px` | 12px |
> | 4 | `--k-space-4` = `16px` | 16px |
> | 5 | **`--k-space-5` = `24px`** | **20px** |
> | 6 | **`--k-space-6` = `32px`** | **24px** |
> | 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24 | not shipped | 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96px |
>
> A layout written against the draft's `space-5` or `space-6` renders larger than intended on
> the shipped tokens. Always read the step's value from the front matter, never from its number.
> Do not add `--space-*` properties. Any renumbering is a breaking change for every consumer.

Layout rules:

- Prioritize outcome and status, reveal evidence progressively, keep provenance accessible.
- Responsive layouts preserve hierarchy rather than merely stacking desktop panels.
- Technical identifiers wrap and copy gracefully.
- Group with cards and panels only when the grouping means something; avoid card soup.
- Final breakpoints are OPEN.

Agents may extend spacing and components responsively when consistent with the tokens and
existing patterns.

## Elevation & Depth

Depth comes from tonal layers first: `--k-bg` → `--k-panel` → `--k-panel-raised`, separated by
`--k-line`. Prefer restrained borders and surface shifts to heavy shadows.

- `--k-shadow` is the soft panel shadow.
- `--k-elevation-overlay` is the single layered shadow for floating surfaces (dialogs, menus,
  palettes, toasts), so elevation tunes in one place.
- `--k-z-*` is the stacking scale; overlays read it instead of inventing local z-index values.

Shadow and stacking values are in `tokens/tokens.css` and listed in the front matter comment.

## Shapes

Do not round everything. Shipped radius roles:

| Token | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `--k-radius-control` | Tight radius for dense controls (inputs, selects). |
| `--k-radius-overlay` | Dialogs, popovers, and other floating surfaces. |
| `--k-radius-sm` | Buttons and badges. |
| `--k-radius-md` | Framed placeholder cards (`.empty--prominent`, `.empty--compact`). |

Shipped `.panel` sets no radius: panels are square-cornered, so do not assume containers are
rounded. `.theme-console` sets `--k-radius-sm` (console) = `0`, `--k-radius-md` (console) = `0`,
`--k-radius-control` (console) = `0`, and `--k-radius-overlay` (console) = `0`.

**OPEN-2 — radius scale.** Shipped: `--k-radius-sm` = `9px`, `--k-radius-md` = `14px`,
`--k-radius-control` = `4px`, `--k-radius-overlay` = `10px`. Draft direction: 6 / 10 / 16 / 24px
as `radius-sm` / `md` / `lg` / `xl`. The names overlap and the values do not; do not add
`--radius-*` properties.

## Components

The shipped primitives (`@kontourai/ui/react`, `@kontourai/ui/elements`) implement these rules;
`docs/explorer-manifest.json` lists each one's states and token contract.

- **Buttons.** Clear primary, secondary, tertiary, and destructive hierarchy. Mapped to the
  shipped variants: primary → `primary`; secondary → `ghost`; tertiary → no shipped variant
  (OPEN); destructive → no defined pattern (OPEN; `negative` is the nearest shipped variant, a
  status-toned button). `positive` and `caution` are status-toned buttons outside the draft's
  hierarchy. Draft rule: the product accent is not automatically the primary action color.
  **OPEN-8:** today `.btn-primary` and
  `--k-focus-ring` are both driven by `--k-brand`, so the accent *is* the primary action and
  focus color. Separate `--k-action` and `--k-focus` roles are
  [#72](https://github.com/kontourai/ui/issues/72); until then, do not work around it with
  local overrides.
- **Inputs** (`Field`, `Input`, `Select`, `Textarea`, `Checkbox`, `Toggle`). Visible labels;
  placeholders are not labels. Validation explains recovery.
- **Cards and panels** (`Panel`). Only for meaningful grouping.
- **Tables.** Optimize scanning, alignment, sorting and filtering, copyable values, and explicit
  statuses. (No shipped primitive yet.)
- **Inspectors.** Preserve context while exposing deeper evidence and provenance. (No shipped
  primitive yet.)
- **Dialogs** (`Dialog`). Reserve interruption for actions that need focus or confirmation.
- **Status** (`Badge`, `StatusBadge`, `StatusBar`). Always include text; icon and color
  reinforce it.
- **Loading** (`Skeleton`, `Spinner`, `Progress`). Communicate useful state without fake
  precision. Never imply completion while work is pending.
- **Empty states** (`Empty`). Explain purpose and the next action.
- **Errors.** State the failure, its impact, recoverability, and the next action; reveal
  technical detail progressively.
- **Iconography.** UI icons use simple geometry, consistent optical weight, thin-to-medium
  strokes, and excellent small-size legibility. Do not turn utility icons into contour art.
  Avoid humanoid robots, glowing brains, floating code, and cyber grids.

## Do's and Don'ts

Token rules:

- Do style with `--k-*` tokens; don't hard-code hex values, font sizes, radii, or spacing.
- Don't introduce the draft's `--kontour-*`, `--space-*`, or `--radius-*` names as CSS.
- Don't assume a step number means the same size in the draft and the shipped scale (OPEN-1).
- Don't use product accents as status, and don't use status tones as identity.
- Don't hand-edit this file's front matter; regenerate it.

Agents **MUST** preserve:

1. the contour and environment metaphor
2. the corporate/product distinction
3. Station's ownership of the S-river
4. each product's unique phenomenon
5. the semantic separation of product color and status color
6. uncertainty → clarity
7. progressive trust inspection
8. flat and monochrome viability
9. accessibility
10. canonical asset authority

Agents **MUST NOT**:

1. put Station's S-river in the company logo
2. add a compass to every product
3. make every product a recolored contour blob
4. introduce generic AI motifs
5. use gradients as a substitute for structure
6. assume concept typography is final
7. redraw canonical SVGs without an explicit identity task
8. invent unresolved brand decisions, or resolve an OPEN item silently
9. hide uncertainty for visual cleanliness
10. reduce provenance to decorative metadata

Agents **MAY** extend spacing and components responsively when consistent with the tokens and
existing patterns. Changes to master marks, the core palette, product semantics, typeface
families, or trust-state semantics are design-system changes and need an explicit decision.

## Marks & Identity

### Corporate mark

The Kontour symbol is a contour field moving from **uncertain → resolved**: one area continuous
and legible, another interrupted, sparse, dotted, or incomplete. Use roughly 4–6 nested paths
from related geometry. Preserve deliberate spacing, small-size legibility, controlled organic
variation, and a distinctive silhouette. Avoid perfect concentricity and decorative noise.

Never add Station's S-river, a compass rose, a literal mountain, a location pin, a checkmark,
shield, lock, brain, neural nodes, circuitry, AI sparkles, a robot, a chat bubble, a generic
hexagon, or an infinity loop to the corporate mark.

### Station

A river or path forming a subtle **S** through a contour environment; the S emerges from the
landscape rather than appearing as a letter. Station-specific: never the corporate mark.
Station communicates orientation, location, arrival, state, inspection, checkpoint, reference,
and reliability. A compass or reference marker may stay Station-specific if simplified,
subordinate, and semantically useful. Do not propagate it to every product. Release channels
(stable, beta, dev, nightly) may use controlled accent variants that keep the geometry; the
channel colors are OPEN.

### Flow

Progression, routing, transfer, orchestration, transformation: work moving through a system.
Use contour-derived directional behavior. A subtle F may emerge naturally; never force a
literal F. Flow must stay distinct from Station at app-icon size.

### Surface

A state, region, layer, or plane made visible: exposed plane, plateau, basin, bounded region,
section, or revealed layer. **See the state clearly.** Surface is not another generic contour
blob; the surface itself is the defining phenomenon.

### Future products

Start with: *what phenomenon in the Kontour world represents what this product actually does?*
Territories such as ridge, field, basin, trace, range, layer, boundary, current, crossing, or
vale are concepts, not reserved names. Before approving an identity, document its function,
phenomenon, semantic mapping, differentiation, shared grammar, 24px behavior, and monochrome
behavior.

### Flat vs. dimensional

Every core mark needs a flat version for navigation, favicons, docs, badges, CLI, and small UI.
Dimensional or cartographic treatment (shallow elevation, subtle shadow, terrain or paper
material, inset paths, restrained depth) is allowed for app icons, launch screens, marketing,
product cards, and presentations. Avoid photorealism. If removing gradients, texture, shadow,
embossing, and color destroys the identity, the mark is unfinished.

Contour artwork belongs in identity, hero moments, explanatory diagrams, meaningful empty
states, and selective launch or loading moments, not behind every card.

### Production assets

Canonical SVG sources are planned ([#75](https://github.com/kontourai/ui/issues/75)):
`kontour-symbol.svg`, `kontour-wordmark.svg`, `kontour-lockup-horizontal.svg`,
`kontour-lockup-stacked.svg`, and a `<product>-symbol.svg` plus `<product>-lockup.svg` for
Station, Flow, and Surface. The product icons shipped in `icons/` today
are the current UI marks. Raster exports derive from SVG; never use generated concept images as
production logo sources. Every finalized mark must pass monochrome, ~24px recognition,
favicon and app-icon, light-mode, dark-mode, no-effects, and applicable contrast tests.

## Motion

Shipped tokens: `--k-ease` and `--k-dur` (values in the front matter comment). Exact durations
and easing beyond these are OPEN.

Preferred metaphors:

- **Resolve:** broken contours become continuous.
- **Trace:** a path progressively reveals.
- **Focus:** secondary layers recede.
- **Traverse:** work moves through a defined path.
- **Layer:** deeper evidence becomes visible.

Avoid random particles, AI glows, constant ambient animation, gratuitous morphing, and motion
that implies completion while work is pending. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Interaction Model

> **Complex underneath. Clear on the surface.**

Progressive inspection: **Outcome → Status → Explanation → Evidence → Provenance → Raw
execution.** Outcome answers what happened. Status states what Kontour can establish.
Explanation says why. Evidence supports it. Provenance shows origins and transformations. Raw
execution exposes model, tool, and event detail.

These are **contours of detail**. Users move between them without losing context.

## Trust UX

Prefer evidence over assertion. Do not merely say **Verified** when the product can explain
what was checked, against what, by what mechanism, and with what limitations. Prefer
"12 cited records matched the extracted values" over "Fully trustworthy."

Where relevant, expose source, actor, model, tool, timestamp, transformation, validation step,
human approval, artifact or result, version, and lineage.

Distinguish **known, verified, inferred, estimated, uncertain, conflicting, failed,
unavailable, and not checked**. Never collapse these into one generic confidence state
(tokens: OPEN-7).

Human review is first-class provenance. Failures state what failed, the impact,
recoverability, retained partial work, and the next action.

## AI & Agent Activity

Do not anthropomorphize routine system behavior. Prefer "Model returned…", "Tool call
failed…", "Kontour verified…", and "3 sources support this value…" over "The AI thought…".

Distinguish planned, running, completed, failed, skipped, retried, human-approved, and
superseded events. Raw traces are not the default explanation: summarize first, inspect
downward.

## Data Visualization

Charts prioritize comparison and interpretation over decoration, and every chart answers a
user question. Never use product identity colors as an implicit status scale. Represent
uncertainty and completeness with multiple cues (labels, line style, shape, opacity, pattern,
and color). Broken/continuous contour logic is allowed only when semantically appropriate.
Provide textual equivalents where needed.

## Voice & Writing

Kontour sounds grounded, clear, precise, human, and optimistic. Avoid hype, fear, grand claims,
excessive jargon, vague intelligence claims, and unsupported certainty. Specificity builds
credibility.

- Prefer "See how this result was produced" over "Unlock unprecedented AI transparency."
- Prefer "Verified against 12 source records" over "AI you can finally trust."

## Accessibility

Accessibility is part of trust. Require keyboard access, visible focus (`--k-focus-ring`),
semantic markup, accessible names, sufficient contrast (`npm run check:contrast` enforces WCAG
AA on the shipped pairs), reduced-motion support, no critical color-only encoding, usable zoom
and reflow, appropriate target sizes, screen-reader-readable status changes where needed,
meaningful table headers, and textual equivalents for charts.

## Design QA Checklist

Before calling a UI or brand task complete, verify:

- Does it make the user's primary outcome clear?
- Can a user tell what Kontour knows from what it infers?
- Is evidence accessible at the appropriate depth?
- Is provenance preserved?
- Are errors and uncertainty explicit?
- Does product identity stay distinct from status semantics?
- Does Station keep its S-river ownership?
- Are contours meaningful rather than decorative noise?
- Are canonical assets reused rather than approximated?
- Does it work in light and dark where required?
- Is important meaning available without color?
- Is keyboard and focus behavior correct?
- Is the hierarchy usable on narrow screens?
- Are technical values copyable where useful?
- Is the copy specific rather than hype-driven?
- Does it use `--k-*` tokens only, and did it resolve no OPEN item by accident?
- Did the implementation introduce a new design-system rule accidentally?
- Does the result feel calm, precise, and inspectable?

## Canonical Direction

Intentional, not up for casual change: the Kontour/contour naming relationship; environmental
product architecture; the uncertainty → clarity metaphor; the corporate contour-field concept;
Station's S-river; product-specific environmental phenomena; a restrained corporate palette;
distinct product accents; "Trust the work AI does."; separation of corporate and product
iconography; the progressive "contours of detail" interaction model; evidence and provenance
as first-class trust UX.

## Final Principle

The visual identity and the product experience express the same idea:

> **Make invisible structure visible.**

Kontour is not trustworthy because it looks secure. It earns trust by making AI work
understandable, attributable, inspectable, and appropriately uncertain.

The contour is not decoration. **It is the model for the product.**
